claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

1. **Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children, and what are their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now, to continue assessing your eligibility:

**Do you live with Alex, or are you paying towards their upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money) at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just one more question to ensure I have all the necessary information:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any special residential accommodation, or do they live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex was in care for a little while - a couple of months - but they're back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. To understand your current situation better:

**How long ago did Alex return home from care, and are they now living with you permanently?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They're living with me now, yes. They've been back home for a bit now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 6 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with you at home
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is currently back home with you after their time in care

Since Alex is now living with you full-time at home, you are responsible for them, and they meet the age requirements, you should be eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Since Alex is 6 years old, lives with you in the UK, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for them, you meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit. The fact that Alex was previously in care for a couple of months doesn't affect your current eligibility now that they're back home with you.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you should do so as soon as possible, as Child Benefit can usually only be backdated for up to 3 months from the date of your claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
